name: Cable Chest Fly
summary: A standing cable isolation exercise that targets the pectoralis major through horizontal shoulder adduction.

setup: Set both cable pulleys at approximately mid-chest height.
Grasp a single-hand handle in each hand with palms facing forward or toward each other.
Step forward into a staggered stance to establish balance, keeping an upright torso with a slight forward lean from the ankles.
steps: Start with your arms extended out to your sides with a slight, fixed bend in the elbows until you feel a comfortable stretch in the chest.
Bring both handles together in a wide hugging arc across the front of your chest until your hands nearly touch.
Squeeze your chest firmly at the peak contraction for a brief pause.
Control the handles back along the same wide path until you reach the stretched position, resisting the cable tension.
instructions.breathing: Inhale as you open your arms and stretch the chest; exhale as you bring your hands together in front.
cues: Squeeze through your chest, not your hands

common_faults.fault: Turning the fly into a press by excessively bending and extending the elbows.
common_faults.correction: Keep a fixed, soft bend in your elbows throughout the entire movement.

common_faults.fault: Overextending the arms backward past the shoulder plane, placing excessive stress on the anterior joint capsule.
common_faults.correction: Stop the eccentric phase when your hands align roughly with your torso and you feel an active stretch in the pecs.

common_faults.fault: Swinging the torso to create momentum.
common_faults.correction: Brace the core, maintain a solid staggered stance, and keep the torso stationary.

precautions: Avoid letting the cables yank the shoulders back beyond an active, comfortable range of motion.
